prompt_template:
Plan a one-day itinerary in <city>, Japan for a traveler with this taste.
Favorite artists: <artists>. Favorite films: <films>. Food they like: <food>.
Give exactly 5 stops (morning, lunch, afternoon, dinner, evening). For each stop give the real place name and its neighborhood, and one sentence on why it fits this traveler's taste.
Answer with JSON only: [{"slot":"morning","name":"...","area":"...","reason":"..."}, ...]

stops.name: Chatei Hatou
stops.reason: This legendary, dimly-lit kissaten serves exquisite hand-drip coffee in a quiet, contemplative atmosphere that mirrors the minimalist, ambient aesthetic of Ryuichi Sakamoto.

stops.name: Sobahouse Konjiki Hototogisu
stops.reason: A Michelin-starred ramen destination crafting complex, innovative clam-infused broths that will satisfy both your ramen craving and your appreciation for avant-garde craftsmanship.

stops.name: Daikanyama T-Site
stops.reason: An architecturally stunning cultural hub where you can browse an incredible selection of design books and rare vinyl, appealing directly to the artistic sensibilities of a Radiohead fan.

stops.name: Omoide Yokocho
stops.reason: This narrow, atmospheric alleyway filled with tiny yakitori stalls offers a moody, neon-drenched dining experience that feels like stepping directly into a cinematic Tokyo film frame.

stops.name: New York Bar
stops.reason: Located atop the Park Hyatt, this iconic jazz bar is the ultimate pilgrimage for fans of 'Lost in Translation', offering melancholic night views of the glittering Tokyo skyline.

stops.name: Kennin-ji Temple
stops.reason: The temple's stunning Zen gardens and graphic 'Twin Dragons' ceiling painting blend spiritual mysticism with a bold visual design that appeals to both Spirited Away and Cornelius fans.

stops.name: Men-ya Inoichi
stops.reason: This acclaimed ramen shop serves meticulously crafted, dashi-based ramen, embodying the obsessive pursuit of noodle perfection celebrated in the film Tampopo.

stops.name: Otagi Nenbutsu-ji Temple
stops.reason: With its 1,200 whimsical, moss-covered stone statues, each with unique and quirky expressions, this temple captures the playful, otherworldly spirit of the deities in Spirited Away.

stops.name: Izuju
stops.reason: This historic establishment specializes in traditional Kyoto-style sushi like sabazushi, offering a nostalgic and deeply authentic culinary experience that fits the food-loving soul of Tampopo.

stops.name: Club Metro
stops.reason: As a legendary hub for Kyoto's underground electronic and indie music scenes, this venue's avant-garde atmosphere perfectly resonates with the experimental, genre-defying style of Cornelius.

stops.name: Fuglen Tokyo
stops.reason: Start your day with world-class specialty coffee in a beautifully designed, mid-century modern space located in the trendy neighborhood that birthed the Shibuya-kei music scene.

stops.name: Tsuta
stops.reason: Experience the ultimate quest for ramen perfection at this Michelin-starred establishment, embodying the obsessive culinary devotion celebrated in the film Tampopo.

stops.name: Tower Records Shibuya
stops.reason: Explore the massive vinyl and release sections of this iconic music store, which features dedicated spaces for Tokyo music legends Cornelius and Ryuichi Sakamoto.

stops.name: Taimeiken
stops.reason: Dine at the historic restaurant where director Juzo Itami famously collaborated to create the iconic, runny 'Tampopo Omurice' featured in the film.

stops.name: Bar Music
stops.reason: Wind down at this intimate, audiophile-friendly venue that perfectly bridges your tastes by serving exceptional coffee and drinks alongside a meticulously curated vinyl soundtrack.
